Advances: ancora.parsing, ancora.gate

Findings: F2 (Critical, data C1), F27 rides along (Medium, data M4). Individual report: 20260904-061300-data.md beside ~/vaults/rmbrs-vault/code_review/critical/ancora/2026-09-04/ancora-xla-post-ship-hardening/20260904-061300-consolidated.md.

Deliverable:
lib/ancora/parser.ex writes nil under "meta" both when a spec-meta block is rejected by the schema (parser.ex:54) and when no block exists at all (parser.ex:88). The ancora-xla.1 fix made lib/ancora/verifier.ex:62 suppress missing-field findings whenever meta is nil so a rejected block yields exactly one spec/parse_error. The absent-block case therefore now yields nothing: a corpus where a subject file has no spec-meta block gets `spec.check result=pass`, `impacted_subjects=` empty, while `checked subjects=1` still counts the file. Reproduced at e18fa05; main crashed loudly (BadMapError in Gate.validate_override_subjects/2) on the same fixture, so the branch turned a loud failure into a green light. Deleting the block from a live subject is caught only incidentally by change/missing_decision. The retirement ADR's reasoning states the bug: it asserts nil means "rejected", but nil also means "never present".
Fix: give rejected metadata its own marker in Ancora.Parser so the verifier can tell rejection from absence, and key add_missing_fields/6's suppression on that marker, not on nil; a file with no block must produce a blocking finding (spec/missing_field for the block itself, or spec/parse_error naming the file; the implementer picks and the spec states it). Count identified subjects, not files, in the `checked subjects=` line (gate.ex:535) so CI output cannot hide the gap.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/ancora/parser_test.exs, test/ancora/verifier_test.exs, test/ancora/index_test.exs, test/ancora/gate_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs
- Behaviors to demonstrate through the real tasks (subprocess), on a fixture whose subject file has no spec-meta block:
  1. `mix spec.check --base HEAD` ends result=fail with exactly one blocking finding naming the file; `mix spec.validate` the same; spec.status/next/prime/review do not crash. Mutation: restore the nil-keyed suppression; the test must fail.
  2. The rejected-block fixtures from ancora-xla.1 (malformed id; omitted status) still yield exactly one spec/parse_error each and no false missing_field. Mutation: key the suppression on absence instead of rejection; those tests must fail.
  3. `checked subjects=` counts identified subjects: 0 on the no-block fixture, 1 when the block is present. Mutation: count files; the test must fail.
- Spec edit required in-diff: ancora.parsing (structural_references or a new scenario under scenario.invalid_spec_meta) shall state that a spec file without a spec-meta block produces a blocking finding naming the file and is not counted as a checked subject; ancora.gate or ancora.tasks shall state what `checked subjects=` counts. Decision-record edit: ancora.decision.invalid_spec_meta Decision section gains the rejected-vs-absent distinction.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: compile-graph-scoped checks only (`mix test --stale` or the named files) plus `mix spec.validate`; run `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` as a dev-loop check as soon as the spec edit exists, before either capped final-tier run.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, the named test files, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix deps.unlock --check-unused`, `mix spec.check --base e18fa05`, run-until-green. Full suite runs at the orchestrator's merge gate.
  - Verifier tier: `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` plus targeted selections; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test that fails under the named mutation; prove each ordered test both ways and report the numbers
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh: the substantive requirement or scenario edit named below lands in the same diff with its decision-record edit; never a Spec-Ack trailer; never weaken a must
  - Fixtures never call production functions (use test/support or System.cmd); under file-scoped derivation a stray call binds a subject
  - Grader scratch discipline applies to you too: work only in this worktree, address it by absolute path
- Call-site Integration: the production path is Parser.parse -> Index.build -> Verifier.verify inside Gate.check/2; prove it through the CLI fixtures, not a unit test of the verifier alone.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/review/**, lib/ancora/trailer.ex, lib/ancora/git/**, lib/ancora/derive/**, lib/ancora/config.ex, lib/mix/tasks/** (moduledocs belong to another child)
Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/parser.ex, lib/ancora/verifier.ex, lib/ancora/index.ex (only if the marker must flow through it)
- lib/ancora/gate.ex (the `checked subjects=` count only)
- test/ancora/**, test/mix/tasks/**, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.parsing.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md (substantive edits named above; never weakening a must)
- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (binding-aware clause: derivation is file-scoped, so acknowledgment edits only, one substantive sentence describing what this ticket changed as that subject observes it, verified by execution; if the subject observes nothing, say so in the completion record and stop)
- .spec/decisions/** (every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; write a real contract statement, never a hollow line)

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do not reintroduce spec/invalid_id for subject ids (the xla.1 contract stands). Do not change the JSON report shape. Do not rebase; base stays e18fa05.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes (`mix spec.check --base e18fa05` result=pass)
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

   that fails when the requirement breaks in a way this ticket's code paths could produce),
   I cannot name one. That makes it a Gap, not a Note. The three-findings-per-file shape is
   also the exact noise ancora.decision.invalid_spec_meta was written to remove, so it is not
   a cosmetic difference.

   Cheapest fix: assert the summary line's error count and the message detail, e.g.
   `assert check.stdout =~ "errors=1 warnings=0"` plus
   `assert check.stdout =~ "missing field spec-meta"`. Either one alone kills the mutation.

2. The absent-block assertion is weaker than its neighbor. Same Gap, folded into 1.
   index_test.exs:261 asserts `check.stdout =~ "spec/missing_field .spec/specs/missing-meta.spec.md"`,
   which pins only the code and the file. The neighboring rejected-block helper
   assert_rejected_meta_line/2 at index_test.exs:359 pins both the `[ERROR] - spec/parse_error
   <file> ::` token and the `field: <field>` detail. The mutation output above demonstrates
   the critic's point concretely: `missing field id` on the same file matches that substring
   exactly as well as `missing field spec-meta` does. Pinning "missing field spec-meta" is
   what separates the block-level finding from a field-level one.

3. The `checked subjects=1` positive control is loose but is a Note, not a Gap.
   index_test.exs:305 is a bare `assert identified.stdout =~ "checked subjects=1"` with no
   exit-status assertion, and the substring would indeed match `checked subjects=10` or `11`.
   The fixture holds exactly one spec file, so no mutation inside this ticket's blast radius
   can produce a two-digit count; the loose match is unreachable rather than merely unlikely.
   The control still earns its place: it is what would catch an over-correction that counted
   zero unconditionally. I would tighten it to `=~ "checked subjects=1 requirements="` for the
   next reader, but it does not change the verdict. Omitting the status assertion is right, not
   wrong — that corpus legitimately still fails for unrelated reasons, so pinning an exit code
   there would over-constrain.

4. Behavior 2 was not loosened. Confirmed.
   The only edit inside the pre-existing rejected-block test is index_test.exs:182,
   `assert spec["meta"] == nil` -> `assert spec["meta"] == :rejected`. Strict equality against
   a specific atom is no weaker than strict equality against nil, and every other assertion in
   that test is byte-identical to e18fa05. Its strength is proven both ways: my mutation 2
   (swap the nil and :rejected clauses) makes it fail 1 of 1 at index_test.exs:192, and it
   passes 1 of 1 on revert. Note that this test does pin the finding count where the new one
   does not — index_test.exs:183 asserts `Enum.map(spec["findings"], & &1.code) ==
   ["spec/parse_error"]` on the raw parser output, no uniq, so a second finding would fail it.
   That is the pattern the new test should have copied.

Verdict: FAIL (unchanged)

Gaps (cumulative, in the order I would fix them):
- ancora.gate.strict_verdict and ancora.parsing.structural_references are false by execution
  for `mix spec.validate`; Ancora.validate/2 at lib/ancora.ex:56 still counts files while
  gate.ex:535 counts identified subjects. Detail in my first comment.
- ancora.parsing.structural_references and ancora.parsing.scenario.absent_spec_meta both say
  "one blocking spec/missing_field finding"; no assertion pins the count or the field name, and
  a fallthrough mutation that emits three findings leaves index_test.exs:234 green.

Notes: the `checked subjects=1` positive control at index_test.exs:305 is a loose substring
with no status assertion, unreachable in this fixture; tightening it to include the following
` requirements=` token would close it. Advisory only.

AUDIT: BOUNCE → implementer
Session: adec463e-8b46-45af-8018-b1cd8b92afc5
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/adec463e-8b46-45af-8018-b1cd8b92afc5.jsonl

Reasoning: I did not inherit the verifier's conclusions. I built my own no-block fixture (git repo, mix.exs, one .spec/specs/missing-meta.spec.md with a spec-requirements block and no spec-meta block) and drove the real tasks from a disposable detached worktree at 50370bf. Both gaps reproduce; both hold. I also measured the remedy end to end before ordering it.

Gap 1 reproduced, verbatim, same fixture, same commit:
  mix spec.check    -> checked subjects=0 requirements=1 errors=1 warnings=0
  mix spec.validate -> checked subjects=1 requirements=1 errors=1 warnings=0
Both lines come from Ancora.Output.checked_summary/1 (output.ex:162) over an index built by the same Index.build/2 call. The divergence is purely the counting expression: gate.ex:535 now reads Enum.count(index["subjects"], &Index.subject_id/1), lib/ancora.ex:56 still reads length(index["subjects"]). Nothing about the validate tier makes a different count correct; the requirements= half of the same line agrees across both tasks.

Remedy: (b), fix lib/ancora.ex:56. Not (a). The two commands print the same line, from the same renderer, over the same index, and a reader has no way to know the number means different things in each. Scoping the sentences to `mix spec.check` would write a stable must that blesses the count lying in the other task, which is the papering-over this ticket exists to stop — and it would narrow a stable must to accommodate a one-line divergence, which is a weakening in substance whatever the wording. The ticket's own motive lands harder on validate: `mix spec.validate` is the command the iteration cadence tells implementers to run, so it is the one whose subject count most needs to not hide the uncounted file. The ticket named gate.ex:535 because that is where its author looked, not because spec.validate was meant to keep counting files.

The remedy is free, and I measured that rather than assuming it. Applying the one line: compiles under --warnings-as-errors, full suite 408 tests 0 failures, mix spec.check --base e18fa05 result=pass (changed_files=8, errors=0 warnings=0, no new drift/growth/shrink). Ancora.Index is already aliased at lib/ancora.ex:12, so the change is the expression and nothing else.

Gap 2 reproduced and it is worse than "the test file misses it". I ran the fallthrough mutation: delete the add_missing_fields(findings, nil, _required, subject_id, file, "spec-meta") clause at lib/ancora/verifier.ex:65 so nil falls to the generic per-field clause. On my fixture that yields three findings instead of one — `missing field id`, `missing field kind`, `missing field status`, errors=3. Under that mutation the ENTIRE suite is green: 408 tests, 0 failures, including all five named test files. Nothing anywhere in test/ can tell one finding from three. spec_finding_codes/1 (index_test.exs:351) ends in Enum.uniq |> Enum.sort so it is a distinct-code set by construction, and the last-line assertion at :263 stops before the errors= token. The defining word in both new spec sentences is "one", and I cannot name an assertion that holds it there.

Bounce reason:
1. lib/ancora.ex:56 counts files while lib/ancora/gate.ex:535 counts identified subjects, so ancora.gate.strict_verdict and ancora.parsing.structural_references (both must, both stable) are false by execution for mix spec.validate, as is the new scenario ancora.parsing.scenario.absent_spec_meta, whose when clause reads "each corpus-reading Mix task".
   Fix: at lib/ancora.ex:56 replace `subjects: length(index["subjects"]),` with `subjects: Enum.count(index["subjects"], &Index.subject_id/1),`. Leave the spec sentences unqualified; they are correct as written once the code agrees.
   Check that proves it: test/ancora/index_test.exs already runs spec.validate on the no-block fixture at :265 and never reads its count. Add, after :269, `assert validate.stdout =~ "checked subjects=0 requirements="`.
   Mutation it must kill: revert lib/ancora.ex:56 to `length(index["subjects"])`. The assertion must fail against the real line `checked subjects=1 requirements=1 errors=1 warnings=0`.
   SCOPE: yes, this needs the orchestrator to widen Allowed touches to include lib/ancora.ex, scoped to the `checked subjects=` count only. It is not in the current list. Do not start item 1 until that grant lands; item 2 is unblocked now.

2. "one blocking finding" is asserted nowhere. No assertion in the repo pins the finding count or the field name for the absent-block case, and the three-findings mutation above leaves all 408 tests green.
   Fix, in the new test in test/ancora/index_test.exs: add `assert check.stdout =~ "errors=1 warnings=0"` and `assert check.stdout =~ "missing field spec-meta"`, and the same two assertions against validate.stdout. The second is what separates the block-level finding from a field-level one: `missing field id` on the same file satisfies the current :261 substring exactly as well as the correct message does, which the mutation output demonstrates concretely. Pin the [ERROR] severity token too while you are there, the way assert_rejected_meta_line/2 (:359) already does for the rejected neighbor — the real line is `[ERROR] .spec/specs/missing-meta.spec.md spec/missing_field .spec/specs/missing-meta.spec.md :: .spec/specs/missing-meta.spec.md: missing field spec-meta; add the required field`.
   Mutation each check must kill: delete the nil clause at lib/ancora/verifier.ex:65 so nil falls through to the generic per-field clause. Both new assertions must fail — errors=3 defeats the count assertion, and the absence of `missing field spec-meta` defeats the detail assertion. Report the numbers both ways.
   The pattern to copy is index_test.exs:183, which asserts Enum.map(findings, & &1.code) == ["spec/parse_error"] with no uniq and so does pin a count.

Notes (not blocking):
- The `checked subjects=1` positive control at index_test.exs:302 is a bare substring with no exit-status assertion and would match 10 or 11. Unreachable in a one-file fixture, so it is not a gap. You are editing this test anyway: tighten it to `=~ "checked subjects=1 requirements="`. I agree with the verifier that omitting the status assertion is correct there, since that corpus legitimately still fails for unrelated reasons.
- Attribution in the three-arm comprehension at index_test.exs:281: `assert result.status == 0, result.stdout <> result.stderr` does not name which task failed. The following heading assertion makes a failure recoverable, so this is cosmetic. Adding heading to the status assertion's message finishes it.
- Correcting one claim in the verifier's own Notes, by execution. It listed a duplicate spec-meta block among the paths that now collect missing_field alongside parse_error. That is wrong: a duplicate block keeps the first block's meta, so the fixture reports `checked subjects=1` with a single spec/parse_error ("spec-meta may only appear once per file") and no missing_field. The non-mapping path does behave as described — a spec-meta decoding to a list yields both `spec parse error — spec-meta must decode to a mapping` and `missing field spec-meta`, errors=2. The second message is untrue of a file that plainly has the block. It blocks either way and no spec sentence forbids it, so it does not belong to this ticket. Worth a follow-up ticket to route the non-mapping and decode-failure paths through the :rejected marker as well.
- Everything else in the diff holds up under my own checks. The marker split is the right shape, the ADR carries the rejected-versus-absent distinction as a real decision rather than a changelog line, and the crash-to-silent-pass-to-blocking-finding progression is real.
